During the Watergate scandal, a spectator holds up a sign at t the Academy Awards red carpet. Los Angeles. 1974

The Watergate scandal was a major political scandal that occurred in the United States in the 1970s, following a break-in at the Democratic National Committee headquarters at the Watergate office complex in Washington, D.C. and President Richard Nixon's administration's attempted cover-up of its involvement. When the conspiracy was investigated by the U.S. Congress, a constitutional crisis developed as it was found that Nixon had entered into a criminal conspiracy. The scandal led to the discovery of multiple abuses of power by the Nixon administration, articles of impeachment, and the resignation of Nixon as President of the United States on August 9, 1974.

Nixon, similar to Presidents before him, had the practice of recording every conversation and phone call he had in his office. One of the mysteries uncovered by the investigation was an 18 1/2 minute discussion that had been taped over. The contents missing from the recording remain unknown to this day but it is widely believed that the tapes recorded a conversation between Nixon and his Chief of Staff H. R. Haldeman.

Apparently since then Presidents have stopped the practice of recording all of the goings on in the Oval Office.
